title: Project Context Pack
description: The living per-project context object that rides along with every event before narration. Sections 1, 2, and 7 are human-owned (set in onboarding interview, rarely change). Sections 3-6 are machine-owned (auto-discovered and continuously updated by events). The narrator reads the whole pack; the router reads mostly section 2.

identity.description: HUMAN-OWNED. The narrator quotes this language back to the user.

name.description: Display name, exactly as the owner says it.

owner_description.description: One sentence in the owner's own words. E.g. 'Loom is where my retailers place orders.' The narrator's vocabulary source.

audience.description: Who uses it, in the owner's words. E.g. 'my 12 retail partners', 'just me', 'paying customers in the App Store'.

stakes.description: HUMAN-OWNED. The single most important section — this IS the router's input. Derived from three plain questions: Does anyone besides you use this? Roughly how many? Does it touch money?

tier.description: sandbox: experiments, break freely. personal: only the owner depends on it. live_small: external users exist but small blast radius. live_critical: real users/revenue depend on uptime.

user_scale.description: Owner's rough estimate. Precision is not the point; blast radius is.

touches_money.description: Payments, invoicing, orders, payroll — anything where an error has financial consequences.

business_role.description: What breaks in the owner's LIFE if this breaks. Drives the users-affected verdict's framing.

downtime_translation.description: Owner-stated consequence of an outage, used verbatim in high-stakes narration. E.g. 'my retailers can't submit orders'.

topology.description: MACHINE-OWNED (human-confirmed once). Maps connector-level resources onto this project so events resolve to the right card. The hardest real-world mapping in the product lives here.

sources.description: Every connected resource that belongs to this project.

connector.description: Extend this enum as connectors ship; never free-text.

resource_id.description: Connector-native ID: repo full name, service ID, DB project ID, bundle ID...

role.description: source_of_truth vs code_mirror is the SILD lesson: which code source is actually current.

serves.description: Other project_ids that depend on this one (e.g. an internal platform managing sibling apps, a shared DB). Lets the narrator say 'this may affect X too.'

consumes.description: Other project_ids this one depends on (webhooks in, APIs called, services awaited). The inverse edge of serves — added when real multi-app stacks proved dependency narration needs both directions ('X's outage may lag sync into this app'; pre-launch: 'this feature is waiting on X').

stack_summary.description: One line of tech context fed to the LLM, not shown raw to the user. E.g. 'Node/Express on Railway, Neon Postgres, Clerk auth.'

capability_gaps.description: For live-but-incomplete projects: features the live product is missing, in plain English. Powers standing gap narration ('day N of a store that can't take orders') rather than event narration. Cleared by the owner or by connector evidence (e.g. first real Stripe charge).

summary.description: Plain-English statement of what's missing and what it blocks.

blocking.description: What this gap blocks: revenue, fulfillment, core feature fidelity...

baselines.description: MACHINE-OWNED. What 'normal' looks like — the source of the two most valuable sentences: 'this is unusual' and 'this happens sometimes, it's fine.' Seeded from history, continuously updated (rolling 30d).

deploy_cadence.description: dormant = no deploys in 30d. A deploy to a dormant project is itself news.

known_flaky.description: Checks/steps that fail intermittently without meaning anything. Narrator downgrades these.

note.description: Plain-English gloss, e.g. 'this test is flaky, usually passes on retry.'

graduated.description: True once confirmed by human feedback or 3+ self-resolving occurrences.

active_hours_utc.description: When the owner usually works on this. Activity far outside it (a 3am deploy) is worth a gentle mention.

state.description: MACHINE-OWNED. Live snapshot, updated by every resolved event. What makes narration situational: 'the previous version is still running' is only sayable from here.

version_ref.description: Commit SHA / deploy ID currently in production.

healthy.description: null = cannot determine. The narrator must say so, not guess.

in_progress.description: Open branches / PRs / running builds. Feeds the 'in progress' bucket.

summary.description: Plain-English gist, generated once and cached.

stalled.description: in_progress items quiet past the stall threshold (default 14d). Feeds the Ideas surface's resurfacing nudge.

last_event_at_by_source.description: Keyed by connector name. Freshness raw material for the trust ledger.

trust.description: MACHINE-OWNED. The SILD lesson encoded: per-source honesty about whether we can believe what we're seeing. The narrator reads this BEFORE speaking.

status.description: stale_suspected: this source is quiet while a related source keeps changing (repo silent, deploys continuing). Narrate WITH the caveat, never confidently from a dead spine.

overall_confidence.description: Worst-relevant-source wins. At 'partial' or 'low', the narrator must disclose uncertainty in plain English.

voice.description: HUMAN-OWNED. How this project speaks to its owner. Per-project because people want live_critical loud and sandbox silent.

detail_level.description: The onboarding preference: 'just tell me what's happening' / 'explain it, let me see details' / 'I know my way around'.

push_threshold.description: What earns an immediate push vs. folding into the morning digest.

glossary_overrides.description: Per-project term preferences graduated from feedback — the flywheel's local layer. Global library lives outside the pack.
